value.rationale: The 2026 random-coefficient bootstrap construction asks how randomness affects dependence between two walks. A weak Brownian limit does not reveal whether entire unscaled trajectories can be matched after finitely many edits. This theorem resolves that precise path-level question, distinguishes annealed equivalence from singularity of every fixed-environment law, supplies a sharp natural optimal transport cost in Hamming geometry, and identifies logarithmic blow-up at parameter endpoints with a sharp exponential temporal tail. These are distinct structural facts, not routine improvements of CLT constants.
